evidence: Judged against the shipped format, per SKILL.md line 65 and quality-checks.md #41. Under that rule the internal annotation 'Likert we dont use in rewardkit' is a known false positive and not a defect. The template itself ships visual criteria as likert with points = 5. (1) Gates: task/tests/gates/render/judge.toml:20 and gates/constraints/judge.toml:20 each have one criterion with type = "binary". scoring.toml keeps render = 0.0 and constraints = 0.0, which meets the contract that gates stay binary (staged-task-contract.md:96). (2) Functional: all 43 criteria in scored/functional/judge.toml (lines 23-405) are type = "binary" with positive weights from 0.5 to 2.5. Each is an observable pass/fail behaviour: a stage move is accepted or refused, a bulk move is all-or-none, undo succeeds or conflicts, an unread count rises by exactly two, a candidate cannot see private notes, data survives a restart. A grep for craft or degree words (clear, readab, quality, craft, appropriate, reasonabl, good, polish) in functional and gate files finds only two kinds of hit. The first is behavioural: judge.toml:263 asks for a 'readable line naming who and what changed', which is a presence test. The second is the binary render gate's 'readable content' (gates/render/judge.toml:23), a usable-shell test that is correct as binary. No degree-of-quality judgement is forced into binary there. (3) Polish: the 5 criteria (polish/judge.toml lines 17-60) are binary. The template's polish criteria are also binary (template polish/judge.toml lines 20, 30, 40, 51). Every task polish row tests a discrete preservation property with a stated failure condition. hro_pol_live_board: draft text, activeElement and scroll are unchanged after a remote move. hro_pol_live_thread: the draft and focus survive an incoming message. hro_pol_earlier_place: the anchor message stays within a few pixels. hro_pol_failed_send: an explanation shows, the text is kept and nothing is sent twice. hro_pol_session_resume: sign-in is required again, drafts are isolated per user and drafts persist. These are pass/fail, not graded craft, so binary fits. polish/prompt.md:14 says to judge 'not visual craft'. (4) Visual: all 5 criteria (visual/judge.toml lines 17-90; hro_vis_type, hro_vis_color, hro_vis_layout, hro_vis_hierarchy, hro_vis_consistency) are type = "likert", points = 5, weight 1.2. Each has a described anchor at every level 5/4/3/2/1 tied to the named surfaces (board, cards, conversation pane, badges, stage markers, unread counts, empty states). visual/prompt.md:12 and :16 define the gate-failure and not-exercised floor as raw Likert 1, normalized to 0. prompt.md:14 avoids deducting the same defect in more than one row and limits scope to desktop, matching the instruction's 'A clear desktop workspace is what matters. We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout'. Craft is likert with anchors and behaviours are binary. Counterexample attempts: (a) A broken app that could pass because of type choice: a dead or static shell scores binary 0 on gates, functional and polish and Likert 1 (normalized 0) on visual (visual/prompt.md:12), so type choice opens no inflation path. A pretty but non-functional app can earn visual Likert points only after passing the server-backed gate setup. The functional floor of 0.05 and the 0.6 weight bound that, and it is row 40/42 territory. (b) A conforming alternative that could fail because of type choice: an app with good but imperfect craft gets 3-4 on graded anchors, not 0. Each polish row is a discrete property that a conforming app satisfies outright. hro_pol_failed_send and hro_pol_session_resume bundle several conjunctive conditions into one binary bar. That is a granularity or independence question under rows 26/40, not a binary-versus-likert mismatch, because each sub-condition is itself pass/fail. Not measured: no configured judge run exists for this candidate (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... absent'). So it is not demonstrated how the frozen judge applies the likert anchors or how RewardKit normalizes them. That likert handling is inherited unchanged from the template (score.py byte-identical) and belongs to the runtime rows (39/40/42 and the full-run records), not to whether types fit the ask, which the source fully establishes. It does not change this row's verdict.
